patient.history_present_illness: Mr. W. is a 58-year-old man with severe alcoholic cirrhosis (Child-Pugh C, MELD 22) who was found confused and combative in his home by his adult son, who called 911. He could not be aroused to follow commands and had large amounts of tarry black stool on his clothing. His son found empty vodka bottles — the patient had been drinking. On presentation, he is hypotensive (BP 96/58), tachycardic (HR 124), and febrile (37.8°C). He has prominent jaundice, caput medusae, large-volume ascites, fetor hepaticus, and bilateral spider angiomata. Melena on rectal exam confirms active upper GI bleed. His neurological exam shows GCS 10 with prominent asterixis, disorientation, and bilateral Babinski signs. His ammonia is 187 µmol/L — markedly elevated.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Hepatic encephalopathy (West Haven grade III-IV), alcoholic cirrhosis (Child-Pugh C, MELD 22) — precipitated by acute upper GI variceal hemorrhage (nitrogen load) plus spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (ascitic PMN 342) plus acute alcohol ingestion (ethanol 168).

differential.key_features: PMN 342, E. coli; treat empirically with ceftriaxone + albumin.
Coagulopathy + likely fall — CT head mandatory and excludes.
Ethanol 168 mg/dL contributes; tolerant alcoholic so cannot fully account for GCS 10; monitor for withdrawal 24-72 h post-stop.
Cr 1.8; reassess after volume/albumin; AKI affects ammonia clearance.
High thiamine-deficiency risk; give empiric thiamine before any dextrose.

optimal_actions.action: Send targeted laboratory studies: CBC, CMP, ammonia, magnesium, lactate, coagulation. Confirms liver dysfunction and screens for precipitants.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Hgb 7.8 with BUN 64 (active GI bleed); ammonia 187; INR 3.2; ethanol 168; K 3.1; glucose 58; cultures sent.

optimal_actions.action: Non-contrast CT head — exclude structural alternate cause of AMS (hemorrhage, large stroke, mass) before any LP.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No hemorrhage — excludes subdural in setting of coagulopathy and likely fall.

optimal_actions.action: Literature/guideline search to confirm West Haven grading, precipitant management, and lactulose/rifaximin dosing (Variceal hemorrhage management; SBP empiric therapy; AASLD/EASL HE precipitants).
optimal_actions.expected_finding: AASLD/EASL 2014 guidance retrieved; West Haven criteria and precipitant-driven management framework confirmed.

optimal_actions.action: Drug-interaction and medication-reconciliation review covering propranolol (HOLD during active bleed/hypotension), lactulose, rifaximin, antibiotics; thiamine before dextrose; flag any CNS depressants (benzodiazepines, opioids, sedating antiemetics, antihistamines) and confirm lactulose/rifaximin dosing in liver disease.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sedating/CNS-depressant medications identified; lactulose and rifaximin reviewed for hepatic dose adjustment.

optimal_actions.action: Diagnostic paracentesis — fever and ascites in obtunded cirrhotic; PMN with culture.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Ascitic PMN 342/mm³, E. coli — SBP confirmed; ceftriaxone 2 g IV + albumin 1.5 g/kg.

optimal_actions.action: EEG — confirm HE pattern (classic triphasic waves expected) and exclude NCSE in obtunded patient. Triphasic waves are classic but non-specific (metabolic encephalopathies broadly); main role is exclusion of non-convulsive status epilepticus where the differential supports it.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Classic generalized fronto-predominant triphasic waves at 1.5-2.5 Hz with anterior-to-posterior phase lag — HE pattern; no NCSE.

optimal_actions.action: Consult hepatology, critical care (grade III-IV HE), and GI for urgent endoscopy and variceal banding — coordinate definitive care, transplant candidacy assessment where applicable.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Hepatology / critical-care guidance integrated into management.

optimal_actions.action: Draw two sets of blood cultures, aerobic and anaerobic, before the first antimicrobial dose
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Growth identifies the organism and its susceptibility; a negative or pending culture does not exclude the diagnosis, and yield falls once treatment has started

optimal_actions.action: Perform a diagnostic paracentesis and send ascitic fluid for cell count with differential, protein and culture, inoculating blood-culture bottles at the bedside
optimal_actions.expected_finding: A polymorphonuclear count at or above 250 cells/mm3 establishes spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, which is a precipitant that must be treated whether or not fever or leucocytosis is present

optimal_actions.action: Send urine for microscopy and culture as part of the infection screen
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Pyuria and bacteriuria identify a urinary source; a negative result removes it from the list of precipitants

useless_tools.rationale: Amyloid PET has no role in HE workup; reversible metabolic encephalopathy is the issue, not Alzheimer pathology.
DaTscan has no role in HE workup; the question is metabolic encephalopathy, not nigrostriatal degeneration.
Early-onset AD genetic panel has no role in HE workup; reversible metabolic encephalopathy is the diagnosis under consideration.

sequence_constraints.reason: In altered mental status, exclude intracranial mass effect / hemorrhage on imaging before LP to avoid herniation risk.

critical_actions: Urgent upper endoscopy with variceal banding — definitive control of nitrogen-load source.
Transfuse PRBC to target Hgb 7-8 g/dL (over-transfusion worsens portal pressures).
Empiric IV ceftriaxone 2 g daily for SBP + bleeding cirrhotic antibiotic prophylaxis; IV albumin 1.5 g/kg day 1, 1 g/kg day 3.
Lactulose enemas q4-6h until oral route safe (300 mL retention enema); add rifaximin 550 mg BID via NG.
IV thiamine 500 mg before any dextrose.
Airway management: intubate if grade IV / GCS <8; aspiration risk extremely high.
contraindicated_actions: Do not prescribe benzodiazepines for anxiety/agitation — they precipitate and prolong HE (use haloperidol or non-pharmacologic measures for agitation).
Do not prescribe sedating opioids — they worsen HE; consider acetaminophen at hepatic-safe dosing for pain.
Do not perform LP before neuroimaging excludes mass effect when the patient has altered mental status.
Hold propranolol during active hemorrhage with hypotension — blunts compensatory tachycardia.
Do not give NSAIDs (renal failure risk in cirrhosis).
Do not start protein restriction — outdated and harms outcomes.
Do not transfuse aggressively to normal Hgb — increases portal pressure and rebleeding.
key_reasoning_points: HE is a clinical diagnosis: West Haven grading + evidence of liver dysfunction + exclusion of other causes of AMS — ammonia level is supportive only and correlates poorly with grade (AASLD 2014).

Precipitant identification is more actionable than the ammonia number: infection (SBP especially), GI bleed, electrolyte disturbance (hypokalemia/hyponatremia), constipation, sedative/CNS-depressant use, dehydration, dietary protein load, renal failure.
Upper GI bleed is one of the most potent HE precipitants — blood in gut is a massive nitrogen load; BUN/Cr ratio elevation supports an upper source.
SBP and variceal bleed coexist in roughly a third of severe HE cases — both must be addressed simultaneously.
Restrictive transfusion strategy (Hgb 7-8) reduces rebleeding in variceal hemorrhage.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute GCS 10 entirely to alcohol intoxication and observe.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Ethanol 168 cannot cause grade III-IV obtundation in a tolerant alcoholic; ammonia 187 + SBP + GI bleed + triphasic-wave EEG confirm HE.
Diagnostic paracentesis is safe in Child-Pugh C with coagulopathy; prophylactic FFP/platelets are not required per AASLD.

metadata.difficulty_description: Straightforward HE: alcoholic cirrhosis with classic grade 3-4 presentation, variceal hemorrhage as precipitant, classic EEG triphasic waves, ammonia markedly elevated — diagnosis is unambiguous
metadata.revision_reason: July 2026 clinical tool review: reviewer 2 asked that the head CT go from REQUIRED to OPTIONAL in hepatic encephalopathy, citing ACG 2026 recommendation 6 ("in patients with cirrhosis and confusion without new-onset focal neurologic deficits, we suggest against routine brain imaging") and writing the indications into the tool description rather than the tier. Applied. All 30 cases were read in full: this one has no focal deficit, no seizure, no trauma, no stated suspicion of intracranial bleeding, and its CT report is normal. The action stays available, and the sequence rule that imaging precedes a lumbar puncture is untouched
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required tools (labs, CT, lit, drug, paracentesis) + EEG + consult; classic precipitant constellation, but simultaneous management of bleeding, sepsis, and HE makes this more than straightforward. Recalibrated up from prior 'straightforward'.
